chunks: "In the off state of the buck, the high side is off and the inductor current has to continue, so it flows through the low side. There are two sub-intervals.
First is the dead time, both gates off, so the current has no channel to flow through and it goes through the low-side FET's body diode.
The diode's anode is the source, which is ground, and the cathode is the drain, which is the switch node, so SW gets pulled to about minus 0.
7 to minus 1 volts, one diode drop below ground. Then the low-side FET turns on and the channel takes over.
The channel drop I times R DS(on) is tens of millivolts, so SW comes up to just under zero.
At the end of the off state the low side turns off again, another dead time, and SW goes back to minus one diode drop.
Then the high side turns on, SW jumps to V in with some ringing, and the body diode, which was conducting, turns off through reverse recovery, which adds a spike.
So the waveform is a roughly 0 to V in square wave with duty D , with a small negative shelf at each transition for the length of the dead time, and ringing at the rising edge.
During the on state the body diode is reverse biased by the full input voltage."
